findings.why: the expected literal is a value THIS test wrote into its own throwaway project moments earlier — `tests/test_config_store_readers.py § Fixture.project` mints a tempdir, writes a `.perry/config.jsonl` out of `STORE_SETTINGS` and a `.perry/config.md` out of `MD_SAYS`, and the assertion is that the reader answered from the first and not the second. Arrived 2026-08-30 with TASK-233.

`semantics` is a changelog `bin/perry-task` carries in its own source. The payload reaches it through a `cwd=ROOT` run, and half one cannot tell a subtree the tool built out of its own constants from one it built out of the project. Editing the changelog SHOULD redden this test.
`2099-01-01` is the value this test wrote into the store four lines earlier. It is the test's own input coming back, not a fact about the project, and it moves when the test moves.

`state_root` is the record this test selected and mutated, so the assertion moves with the test. The `setting/` half of the key IS read out of `.perry/config.md` — the coupling instance 6 died of — but it names a record the test chose rather than the whole register.

the literal is the value the test itself wrote four lines earlier — it sets state_root to 'docs' and then asserts the rendered line reads '- State root: docs'. Its only live dependency is that the real config HAS a `- State root:` bullet, which is the shape under test rather than a census of what the project holds. Same class as the two other test_md_store false positives above. Arrived 2026-08-21 with TASK-122, after this floor was first recorded.
